analysis.title: US Semiconductors: Peak Rates, Trough Semis: The Pain Needed to Reset the AI Cycle
key_insights: BofA sees peak rates as a necessary condition for a durable SOX trough because rates now affect AI demand, not just semi multiples.
CSP cash burn is expected to worsen from about $140bn in CY26 to $361bn in CY27 per consensus, with the 10-yr near 5% and further Fed tightening possible.

US cloud capex runs about $1.2Tn annualized vs about $1.5Tn+ expected in CY27. Holding spend at the current run-rate implies a ~20% CY27 capex haircut (~30GW vs ~40GW) and up to 35-40% downside to AI semi EPS.
Higher rates raise WACC, weaken marginal project IRRs and make external financing costlier, which could push lower-return projects out of the buildout and make the cycle healthier.
Chip companies are not expected to call the turn first, since semis are downstream of customer capital allocation. Waiting for NVDA/AVGO to guide cautiously is likely waiting too long.
Historically the SOX bottoms 2-6 months before fundamentals and then rallies about 42% on average. The signal sought is lower capex/EPS estimates that stop lowering stock prices.
Watch early-CY27 CSP capex/FCF guidance and TSMC's CY27 capex as the CY28 demand signal.
The SOX has fallen 36% in 150 days from the 6/22/26 peak of $14,635 to $9,420, more than every prior downturn except 2022, while the S&P 500 is down only 4%.
Q3'26 SOX quarterly EPS was a record $129.49, up 122% y/y, while the SOX closed at $9,525, 35% below peak. Price is again leading EPS.

Positioning: defend near-term with lower direct AI-capex beta (TXN/ADI, selectively CDNS/SNPS). Once peak rates, capex reset, quantified EPS cuts and stocks holding converge, rotate first to NVDA/AVGO, then connectivity/optics and semicap.
Total CSP FCF is forecast at ($140bn) in CY26E, ($361bn) in CY27E and ($86bn) in CY28E. Hyperscale FCF turns positive at $23bn in CY28E, which could ease funding/ROI concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: Peak rates plus quantified capex and EPS cuts can set the multiple and earnings floors, and the SOX historically rallies about 42% after troughs.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher rates could break capex, with a ~20% CY27 capex haircut and 35-40% AI semi EPS downside, and EPS may keep falling after the price low.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stocks continuing to fall despite quantified capex and EPS cuts, or no peak-rate visibility.
